title: 2006 AMC 8 Problem 7
statement: Circle \(X\) has a radius of \(\pi.\) Circle \(Y\) has a circumference of \(8 \pi.\) Circle \(Z\) has an area of \(9 \pi.\) List the circles in order from smallest to largest radius.

solutions.text:
Recall that \(C = 2 \pi r\) and \(A = \pi r^2.\) Using these formulas we get that the radius of \(Y\) is \[ 8 \pi \div (2 \pi) = 4. \] We also get that the radius of \(Z\) is \[ \sqrt{9 \pi \div \pi} = 3. \] As \(\pi\) is greater than \(3\) and less than \(4,\) the correct order is \(Z,\) \(X,\) \(Y.\)

Thus, the answer is B .
hints: Convert all three pieces of information into radii.
Use \(C=2\pi r\) for circle \(Y\) and \(A=\pi r^2\) for circle \(Z\).
